headline: Park Entry Pass and Camping Requirements
reservation: Indiana Dunes National Park requires a per-vehicle entry pass, which can be purchased at the Visitor Center or West Beach entrance. The Dunewood Campground requires advanced reservations through the federal portal; sites are not available for walk-ups during the summer. Note that the adjacent Indiana Dunes State Park is a separate entity requiring its own entry fee and distinct reservation system for its campground.

days.title: Dune Successions and Skylines

stops.name: West Beach Succession Trail
stops.detail: Climb the boardwalk stairs for views of the Chicago skyline and the transition from sand to forest.

stops.name: Diana of the Dunes Overlook
stops.detail: Visit the site commemorating local conservation history with views of the expansive foredunes.

days.driving: Allow 30-45 minutes; traffic near Gary can be heavy.
days.note: Stairs on the Succession Trail are numerous; allow time for frequent breaks in the sun.

days.title: Biological Diversity and Wetlands

stops.name: Cowles Bog Trail
stops.detail: Hike the 4.7-mile loop through marshes and swales to a quiet, secluded beach.

stops.name: Great Marsh Overlook
stops.detail: Spot migratory cranes and herons from the accessible birding platforms.

days.note: Mosquitoes are active in the bog during summer; seasonal wetlands may flood lower trail sections.

days.title: Mid-Century History and High Dunes

stops.name: Century of Progress Homes
stops.detail: View the five historic 1933 World's Fair houses relocated to the dunes.

stops.name: Mount Baldy
stops.detail: Visit the park's largest moving dune; access to the summit is restricted to ranger-led walks only.

stops.name: 3-Dune Challenge
stops.detail: Ascend the three highest dunes at the adjacent State Park for a physical landmark hike.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes; covers the eastern end of the park.
days.note: Mount Baldy's summit is often closed for safety; check current access status at the Visitor Center.

intel.title: West Beach Logistics
intel.text: The West Beach lot is the largest in the park and rarely fills, but a fee is required during summer months. Smaller lots like Porter Beach fill by 10 AM on weekends.

intel.title: Reliable Coverage
intel.text: Most park areas have excellent signal due to the surrounding suburban infrastructure. Some low-lying swales near Cowles Bog may have intermittent reception.

intel.title: Highway Services
intel.text: Fuel and supplies are abundant in Chesterton and Michigan City, both located within 10 minutes of the park. No services are located inside the federal boundary.

intel.title: Peak Season Crowds
intel.text: June through August is peak season; mid-week visits significantly reduce wait times at the entrance stations. Fall brings hawk migrations and quieter trails.

intel.title: Railway Transfers
intel.text: The South Shore Line provides access to the park via the Dune Park station. Check the train schedule for transit between Chicago and the dunes.

plan.arrival: Pickup at MGC; check-in at Chesterton or Dunewood Campground after securing beach supplies in Michigan City.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are appropriate for all public roads. Parking for large RVs is limited to Dunewood and West Beach lots.
plan.goldenHour: Lakefront Drive in Beverly Shores for sunset views over Lake Michigan; expect vibrant colors in October.
